forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

payload.statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q). For any parameter u and integer k>=0, let (u;q)_k:=∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-u q^j), and let (u,v,w;q)_k:=(u;q)_k(v;q)_k(w;q)_k. Let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial, and define M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Define U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}), define T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k, define R_{d,r,n}(q):=[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}, and define G_{d,r,n}(q):=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)). Then G_{d,r,n}(q) is divisible by M_n(q) in the Laurent polynomial ring Q[q,q^{-1}]. Equivalently, there exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q).

result_payload.proof_summary: I could verify only the denominator-clearing part: for each k, (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k = \prod_{j=1}^k (1-q^(2dj)) = (q^d;q^d)_k \prod_{j=1}^k (1+q^(dj)), so after multiplying the k-th summand of T_{d,r,n}(q) by U_{d,n}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^(dj)), all denominator factors are cancelled because k\le n-1. Hence G_{d,r,n}(q)=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) is indeed a Laurent polynomial. However, the substantive claim that M_n(q)=[n]_q\Phi_n(q)^2 divides this Laurent polynomial is exactly the deep q-congruence/theorem-level content, and no admissible trusted declaration or lemma establishing that divisibility was provided.
